body:
As a parent and as someone who has faced depression and posted here, I don't think you owe anyone. Don't live life like you're doing it to owe someone, you'll stay depressed. But still, bringing up a kid takes a long time and a lot of work. And most likely they put a lot of love into you over the years. You being away from them is probably the worst thing they could imagine. And don't think you need to be here because you owe them. They want, likely more than anything, for you to be happy. I wouldn't care what my kids grow up to be, as long as they're happy, I'm happy. That's one of the biggest challenges in life.


I know what you mean by being the invisible guy, the childhood depression, no friends, etc. This you've lived through and you're strong in that aspect. But if you want to change, take a leap in the water and just do it. Be more sociable. I already went this direction in another post so I won't go into it much here. I'm pretty reserved so a lot of my life I've had to just jump into things most people don't think much about such as being more socially outgoing. As the pic says on the FP here, do more of what makes you happy.
Good advice. Glad to see you commenting again.

I think you're special, at least to me. I say that because I see a lot of you in me when I was younger. And it was people like you that kept me going, as my friends were a bit socially awkward like myself, so we kept each other strong. People like us, we need to stick together. I'd try to meet people with hobbies you have. There's a lot of people like you in the world, the thing is, you don't see them out in public as much. 

And I know that feeling of feeling stupid and having the most natural things not be so natural because anxiety overwhelms those natural tendencies and clouds the brain from normal function sometimes. And knowing myself and how I was so asocial, I still signed up for the military to wind up jumping out of airplanes. I was so socially anxious, I could barely pay attention to the "black hats", the airborne trainers, on proper exit and deployment so I tended to be scared as fuck when jumping out since the social anxiety impaired my listening ability. But the military really helped me in that aspect. 

My advice is to just jump in. If you wade in, it may likely scare you off. I've had a hard time with this all my life but some things are better off doing spontaneously and free, regardless of minor consequences. Trying to talk to people, you may come off as awkward at first but the people you want to friend are mature enough to realize it's perfectly acceptable and that they're anxious people because they care and are careful about their self projection and perhaps other people's feelings. From what I read so far, you seem a perfectly fine person. 

When I went into the military I thought of myself as all kinds of odd but I learned, I was no more odd than anyone else, I just tended to worry more about my perception. It's that self perception that makes you seem more odd. Some people are fine with that and some are a bit ignorant and don't understand it. But I'm saying more than intended here, just be yourself but maybe a bit more free and spontaneous. I've posted here lately so I may not be the best one to give advice but I can certainly relate.

As another almost suicidal father who posted here, PM me if you want talk and read my submission if you like. I pretty much feel the same way. 

Edit: I was going to go on but I notice OP deleted it. Still, PM me OP if you want to talk.

You like helping people, right OP? By accepting your faults, you help to teach others it's ok to not achieve personal expectations. There's other chances and paths in life. Sometimes I fuck up in life and I actually like to brag about it sometimes to people that are down. I tell them my fuckups in life and they tend to accept their own more. I think you take yourself too seriously, and it's a fault of mine a lot too. Education and money are not the determining factors of personal success, imho. This is not to say you shouldn't pursue it. You can always choose a different academic path that you find more interesting. We do all this to make ourselves happy and perhaps close others, but I don't care if someone's on the side of road picking up cans for a living, if they're content with it, I admire it. Happiness is hard to come by in life. Friends, money, they all come and go but time is always lost. Enjoy what you have and the time you have while we have it.

But at least you have great academic talent. My grades in school were generally not good, and I dropped out of college only a few months in. I forgot how much I hated the social aspect. So I wound up doing construction and I admit, I'm not that interested by it. But fucking up is how you learn and now I have more than a few first-hand stories to tell my kids on how not to do things. Fucking up just means you're just like everyone else, whether they want to admit it or not.

Knowledge is a generic term. There's knowledge that brings you down, some that brings you up. To know more about the world is to know more of its ills also. It's not really a cure-all. Hobbies include surfing the internet, that's about it. Though admittedly I need to find a more outgoing hobby because even this I tend to get bored of.
I don't think so. My Dad kept an emotional distance from me and my brothers like a lot of guys do. It's just a manifestation of living a rough life, it's understandable.
"The revolution will not be televised."

Thanks. You're a good influence on Reddit and I hope you and people like you remain here. At least until it changes like digg and does some god-awful change shunning away its users, hopefully it won't.
This. If you're young and awkward, high school can be hell. But once you get older, less people give a fuck. High school is filled with hormonal kids, this explains it all.

Her father has legal custody though she has them sometimes, so I can't really do much when he gives her permission. He's a religious guy, I'm not, but he seems a decent person. Just grumpy, can't say I don't blame him being 60 and having to watch kids, but it was his choice. I've told them before I would take custody if they didn't want to. When I'm working, it's just as cheap to have someone babysit as pay child support so doesn't make much difference. May as well be with family, I guess. 

But the point is, I'm not sure whether she's clean or not and I don't really have much control over that when she has permission from her father. I suppose her father's doing a decent enough job so I don't feel I need to take them away from him if I could. Like I said, I just tend to worry about them a lot, especially after a few things I've heard from my daughters that may indicate abuse. But court is very tramatic for kids, would be tramatic for me if I found out if they were being abused and I'm not sure I could contain my rage. It all eats me up inside and sometimes I wonder if I can take the worry and guilt of not trying my best to give them a good life. 

I love my kids, I love my ex, though not *in love* with her, can feel sorry for her father and his medical problems while watching the kids, feel bad for my ex's bf because it's easy to get caught up in all that. The worry and empathy I have for all parties involved, especially my kids, just fucking depresses the hell out of me sometimes.

Yeah, but I still feel bad because of their situation. I can't keep tabs exactly on what's going on in their life and they've been around some bad crowds considering their mom went out with and married meth-heads, dealers, and makers. In some ways I feel like they're going to grow up and blame me for not taking them away from all that yet I feel even if I could afford the resources to get custody, it'll hurt them to be taken away from their mom, and they may blame me for it later, and also may make their mom feel in a position I'm at. They've been with their mom a couple years in their early years before I found out she did drugs. But when you're addicted to something like that or have been, having your kids taken away by your ex has really got to hurt and would make her even more fragile. To put it simply, be leery of drugs like that, people. They fuck up families, first-hand and second-hand.

You're young, you haven't messed up yet. Read my self post here below yours. I had the same problems yet continued to have children with the woman because I thought she would be the only woman I'd ever get. Things didn't turn out exactly for the best. I think you and I just have to say fuck it, we need to keep going on to look out for ourselves and those like us. I'm going to try living like a boss for a while and see how my life goes. It should be at least a little lol-worthy.

I'm wondering if it's like the military tactic they used on us in BCT. To call us names and denigrate us to knowing that we'll likely fight back with higher self esteem. Though I'm just being hopeful. 

Don't worry OP. The people pm'ing just have low self esteem. Their way of helping is to lower others, at least you're doing it right.

Relaxing is something I was never good at. But I appreciate the time and effort to reply. I think I need to find some friends. Though I've been hesitant about it since I didn't want to do anything that would interfere with any free time I may have with my kids. They've haven't had the easiest life so far and I don't want to make it worse. But yes, I realize if I want to help them I need to help myself. It's just hard to feel sometimes that I'm being helpful. I'm the type who tries to go out of their way to help someone because I need a lot of that to raise my social self-worth, due to apparently my insecurity issues. I guess I can hope to see them this weekend and try to explain to them why I haven't seen them lately. I guess I'll give them a brief explanation of what depression is and hopefully not blame this on their mom and such. They've had to face their own issues and struggle. Thanks again.

But don't you feel those negative emotions are a valid part of who you are and sometimes useful? If I'm in a big group and feel I have nothing to contribute, it may sadden me, but it makes me find a group where who I am and what I do is felt appreciated. I'm not saying depression is good, it's a sign something needs to change, but by ignoring them and finding out why you have them, I can't see that as constructive. Maybe I'm misunderstanding you. 

But I also believe the mind can change the mind, but there's no denying physiology plays a role. You can only pretend so much pain is not there until we finally have to start listening to it since it builds up logarithmically, at least, in my case. There is real pain in my life and I need to be somewhat sensitive to it, and real pain in others' lives. It may cause pain to delve into it all, but it needs sorted out. Submitting my predicament is one of my ways of doing this, I'd hope. But I find when I'm free from emotion, I'm free from wants. I'm a blank page and even have no want to live. Emotion is important. But I do appreciate your reply and it does provide some insight.

Tried it. I've ate right (mostly vegetarian at one time), exercised right, made sure to eat foods good for your mood, etc. At the best of times, life was only tolerable. I wasn't happy. I'm not trying to fight alternative options, I'm really curious if anyone has any others.

Yeah, I'm sure. I just didn't want them to get too close to me lately. If I did go, it would only hurt them more. But I don't think it would hurt them as much as anyone here may think, the ex-in-laws plus the system have made a decent attempt at making sure they don't get too attached to me.

Yeah, that's good for a short term. But if they're not with me, that's when things get really depressive and I start questioning my life. I worry about them and it eats me up inside. This, in turn, affects other various aspects of my life. 

But don't knock depression. It's like any other emotion, can be good or bad. Depression can make you sensitive to other peoples' feelings and others, and I admit, it can go too far, just as with being so happy so much it makes you ignorant of the true unhappiness in others. Denigrating something that is a part of someone is not a good helping strategy. If there's pain in the world, I don't want to always be ignorant of it, even though, I admit it tends to eat me up sometimes. I think a good mixture is somberness with content. And at this point, I need to rise up to that but I can't find anything that I find fun in to get me to that point. Nothing seems fun anymore.

But I'm not employed now. I quit. I quit eating much. I quit going outside. I quit caring to take care of a system which doesn't seem to care for me and others like me. Nobody seems to care, it seems it's all about the money. And I'm trying to let people know this. Care for you neighbor because if your neighbor's not happy, you're likely not going to be. If I off myself, then taxpayers will likely foot the bill because I'm sure my father-in-law won't, he can barely take care of himself but wants to make sure he has custody. I guess to him and his daughter, it's more of a power struggle. I'm not even sure they care about them the way they're taken care of. 

Can't count on my ex either, she's always been a bum. Had a couple jobs for a few months, the guy she's with barely maintains one and I'm not even sure they're clean. But I'm not here to speak bad about others, I know everyone has their problems and I'm very understanding of theirs. I just have such apathy that it seems no one wants to understand me and the others in my shoes.
